title: Note: reading a ghost story, part 2
summary: The story continues: noticing something, a verb that joins two clauses, and a sudden but.

blocks.text: Part 2 of the ghost story. Misaki walks on, and something is wrong. Read each sentence first, then see what it teaches.

blocks.jp: 美咲は、駅への道を間違えたことに気づいた。
blocks.en: Misaki noticed that she had taken the wrong road to the station.

blocks.jp: 美咲は立ち止まり、あたりを見回した。
ところが、さっきの古い家が、また目の前にあった。
blocks.en: But there was the old house from before, right in front of her again.

blocks.jp: 戸が開いている。美咲は寒さのあまり、そのまま中に入った。
blocks.en: The door is open. From sheer cold, Misaki went straight inside.

blocks.jp: 奥の部屋の戸を、ゆっくり押す。
blocks.en: She pushes the door of the back room, slowly.

blocks.text: 気づく: what you notice is a target

気づく is 気 (spirit, attention) + 付く (to stick). Your attention sticks to something, so what you notice is a **target**, and it takes **に**, not を. The same idea is behind 気をつけて, "be careful". Here the thing noticed is a whole clause turned into a noun with こと.
道を間違えたことに気づいた。 (She) noticed that she had gone the wrong way.
In 立ち止まり、見回した, the first verb is in its い-stem (立ち止まる → 立ち止まり). The い-stem can join clauses in narration, a bit like the て-form but more written and brisk. Both verbs share the zero carriage.
ところが: but at that point
ところが joins ところ (point) and が (but). It means "but at that point": the story turns, and something unexpected is met.
そのまま, and the present tense again

そのまま is the unchanged condition from lesson 42: she went in without changing anything, as she was. And once more the last sentence slips into the present tense (押す) to make the scene feel as if it is happening now.

rows: 道を間違えたことに気づいた
blocks.title: Phrase → lesson it comes from

items: 気づく takes に: the thing noticed is a target.
The い-stem can join clauses in narration.
ところが marks a turn in the story.
Narration may slip into the present tense for effect.
